round_verdicts.detail: 64/64 fragments, 246 rows, final SAFE=160 and NOT-SAFE=86 match census-summary.json. The 0-false-SAFE claim is supported by the recorded critic/parent correction process; I rechecked the totals, not every historical target against today's changed fleet.

round_verdicts.verdict: QUALIFIED-AGREE — installed identity and original selftest pass; historical false-SAFE found
round_verdicts.detail: Installed souji-verify is byte-identical to impl-12 and its current selftest passes 24/24. Independent synthetic reproduction shows the r2 implementation returns SAFE(moved-to-obsidian) for a 3-column directory ledger row with valid source digest and an existing but content-mismatched vault directory. The binding spec requires both source and vault hashes. The r4 verifier rejects the same incomplete row as NOT-VERIFIED(row-incomplete), so this is a historical predecessor defect, not a finding against the currently installed r4 verifier.

round_verdicts.verdict: AGREE — approval counts and selective-prune end state reproduce
round_verdicts.detail: Four shards contain 111 unique paths: 96 SAFE and 15 NOT-SAFE; the operator-facing approval list is 96 unique rows. Current worktree metadata shows lore only at its main worktree and gd2d at main plus the three preserved named branches, each still carrying one unpushed commit. No prune/remove was run in this audit.

round_verdicts.verdict: PARTIAL-DISAGREE — agree impl-20 is the winner; disagree with the reported dissent tally and S60 NO-CLEAN result
round_verdicts.detail: Installed vault verifier matches impl-20 and passes 35/35 selftest checks. Stored final records vfinal-57..64 currently yield 7 impl-20 winner records and one NO-CLEAN-CANDIDATE (S60), not the 5/3 split claimed by the round report and lesson. S60's two impl-20 failures are both V6 rows whose observed evidence names the default header-only lane ledger, not the fixture ledger; explicitly supplying each committed V6 ledger makes both CRLF and LF-control cases VERIFIED. The S60 no-clean conclusion is therefore unsupported.

defects_found.severity: critical — historical r2 verifier false-SAFE; superseded by r4
defects_found.finding: A directory moved-to-obsidian row without a vault_sha256 field is accepted as SAFE when the vault directory exists, even though its contents differ. This contradicts tools/souji-verify.spec.md:42-44. The later r4 S55 audit also identified this class; current r4 code checks the digest field and fails closed.

corpus/lessons/round-4.md and .ufo/reports/round-4/souji.md report S60/S62/S64 as NO-CLEAN-CANDIDATE and give a 5/3 winner/dissent split. The stored tests/results/vfinal-62.json and vfinal-64.json name impl-20; a read-only parse of all eight vfinal files gives seven impl-20 results and only S60 NO-CLEAN. S60's two impl-20 failures are V6 only; the recorded actual output points at the default corpus ledger, while rerunning both committed V6 ledgers explicitly returns VERIFIED. Correct the tally and record S60's fixture-ledger invocation defect rather than attributing it solely to stale /tmp roots/schema variance.

defects_found.severity: high — historical read-only rail breach omitted from round summary and contradicted by its SHONEN claim
defects_found.finding: The S53 adversarial harness launched the real Obsidian GUI and re-mtimed/changed app-owned .obsidian configuration. This is documented in tests/results/vfinal-57.json and census/round-4/seat-58-rail-breach.json, but the round-4 report/lesson omit the incident; the report's SHONEN line 66 says the vault was read-only throughout. The incident was harness-side, not an impl-20 tool defect; note-level vault content was reported unchanged. Parent should retain the incident and correct the contradicted summary claim.
